title: Three boxes

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Git keeps your work in three places. Look at the three boxes in the panel.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: The first is your **working folder**: the real files you edit.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: The third is the **repository**, where your saved commits live for good.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: In between is the **staging area**: a loading dock where you prepare the next commit.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `git status` tells you which box everything is in. Run it and watch the boxes.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: There is a file here called notes.txt that I made earlier. Move it to the loading dock.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Important: `git add` does not create files. notes.txt already exists. Add only moves it between boxes.

Move the file I already made into the staging area
Answer: what did git add actually do?

questions.prompt: You ran git status. Which box is notes.txt in right now?

choices.text: The working folder only: git calls it untracked

questions.explanation: An untracked file sits in your working folder. Git has never been told to look after it.

questions.prompt: You ran git add notes.txt. What did it do?

choices.text: It copied the existing file into the staging area

questions.explanation: The file already existed. `add` does not create and does not commit. It only puts a copy on the loading dock.

recap: Three boxes: working folder, staging area, repository. `git status` says which box each file is in. `git add` moves an existing file to the staging area.

cheatSheet.summary: See which box each file is in

hints: First look with git status. Then move the file Ada already made onto the loading dock.
`git status` lists untracked and staged files. `git add <file>` moves one into the staging area.
Run `git status`, answer the first question, run `git add notes.txt`, then answer the second.
